paragraphs: The Discovery TDV6 was introduced with the D3 generation in 2004, replacing the Td5 diesel that powered the earlier Discovery 2. It's a 3.0-litre V6 diesel — shared across a range of Land Rover and Jaguar models of that era — and was carried through to the D4 facelift, where it was sold alongside the higher-output SDV6 variant. The TDV6 remained in production until the Discovery 4 was replaced by the D5/L462 generation in 2017. The engine is known for its smooth power delivery, but the TDV6 family has a well-documented pattern of timing chain and bearing wear over time — which is exactly what our rebuild service addresses.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace TDV6 engines for every Discovery TDV6 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre V6 diesel fitted to the Discovery from 2004 to 2016 across two generations. Known for timing chain tensioner wear, injector seal leaks, and crankshaft bearing failure risk over time — see the callout above. We replace timing chain components, injector seals, and gaskets as standard on every TDV6 rebuild. Check Your TDV6 Discovery → [link to quote form]

compatibility.intro: Because the TDV6 was fitted across both the D3 and D4 generations, with changes to engine management and ancillaries over the run, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming a part from a later D4 will work on an earlier D3 — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick.
